title: BUILD-GV2-081-privacy-safe-identity-resolution-policy
universal_lens: The privacy-safe identity resolution policy defines a constrained equivalence relation on user event streams. It partitions high-dimensional behavioral data into disjoint sets, maximizing cross-session continuity while strictly bounding information leakage, establishing a rigorous topological foundation for safe analytics without altering the underlying production metric spaces.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this policy acts as a conformal filter over latent player and fan embeddings. By restricting the observable sigma-algebra to anonymized clusters, we ensure Bayesian posterior updates remain robust against adversarial re-identification, maintaining strict calibration of predictive sports intelligence models under evolving regulatory priors.
gse_mapping: For GSE, the primitive dictates state transitions in the situational reasoning engine. It enforces a deterministic mapping from raw telemetry to sanitized context vectors, ensuring that real-time decision-making layers operate exclusively on privacy-compliant manifolds, preventing any leakage of sensitive PII during dynamic game-state evaluations.

The derivation of the privacy-safe identity resolution policy begins by defining the raw event space \mathcal{E} generated by Galaxy Sports Edge users. To prevent re-identification, we introduce a projection operator P that maps \mathcal{E} to a coarser-grained cluster space \mathcal{C}. The core mathematical constraint is an upper bound on the mutual information I(X; Z) between the true identity X and the resolved pseudonym Z, formalized as I(X; Z) \leq \epsilon. This ensures that even with complete observation of the resolved identities, an adversary gains bounded information about the underlying user. Simultaneously, the system must respect a strict dependency graph, modeled via the indicator function G_{dep}, which gates the execution of this resolution layer until foundational primitives (NEXT-001, BUILD-GV2-076) are verified. Furthermore, the operational domain is restricted by a hard boundary condition \Omega_{safe}, explicitly excluding production-critical files like billing and live affiliate modules. The dualities emerge between utility (maximizing cross-session tracking accuracy) and safety (minimizing \epsilon and enforcing \Omega_{safe}). Failure modes manifest primarily as boundary violations—where sandbox mutations leak into \mathcal{F}_{prod}—or information theoretic breaches where \epsilon is poorly calibrated, leading to accidental PII exposure. The resulting framework provides a mathematically rigorous, docs-first implementation strategy that guarantees zero-touch to live revenue systems while enabling advanced analytics.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage to the foundational works of Shannon on information theory and the modern formulation of Differential Privacy by Dwork et al. Historically, identity resolution relied on fragile deterministic hashing, which failed under the scrutiny of GDPR and CCPA. The shift toward probabilistic, bounded-information mappings reflects a broader evolution in quantitative systems from exact state tracking to robust, noise-resilient inference, heavily influenced by cryptographic zero-knowledge proof architectures.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model three primary agents: the System Architect, who seeks maximum analytical granularity; the Compliance Officer, who demands absolute isolation of PII and production stability; and the Adversary, attempting to reverse-engineer identities from cluster assignments. The policy acts as a Nash equilibrium, satisfying the Architect's need for continuity (via \mathcal{C}) while strictly penalizing the Adversary's success probability (via \epsilon) and protecting the Compliance Officer's boundaries (via \Omega_{safe}).
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: An anti-collinearity veto is triggered if the identity resolution clusters \mathcal{C} become highly correlated with sensitive attributes not explicitly permitted, indicating a leakage channel. Furthermore, if the dependency gate G_{dep} evaluates to false but downstream analytics attempt to query unresolved entities, a hard state-transition veto halts the pipeline. This prevents the propagation of undefined or unsafe states into the GSE situational reasoning layers, ensuring strict decoupling between experimental growth OS logic and live financial infrastructure.
